title: Responsive Images
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of responsive images in a browser document.
Apply at least one relevant rule from this lesson to a small HTML example.
Check the result using browser inspection, a validator, or an accessibility checklist.

content.intro: Responsive image markup gives the browser options to select a suitable resource for screen size and pixel density, while preserving a reliable fallback.
content.why_it_matters: Text, links, lists, images, and media are the building blocks of readable, navigable web content; the markup should communicate meaning even before CSS is added.

content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: Text, links, lists, images, and media are the building blocks of readable, navigable web content; the markup should communicate meaning even before CSS is added.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Responsive image selection lets the browser choose an appropriate resource for the viewport and pixel density. Provide a valid fallback image and verify every referenced file or URL.

items.title: What responsive images are
items.text: Responsive image selection lets the browser choose an appropriate resource for the viewport and pixel density. Provide a valid fallback image and verify every referenced file or URL.

items.title: The srcset attribute
items.text: The srcset attribute: a list of candidate image resources and descriptors from which the browser can select.

items.title: The sizes attribute
items.text: The sizes attribute: a description of the image’s expected rendered CSS width at different viewport conditions.

items.title: Resolution switching
items.text: Resolution switching is one of the decisions covered by Responsive Images. Decide what the markup is meant to communicate, choose the native HTML structure that expresses that meaning, and verify the result in a browser or a relevant validation checklist. Avoid using an element or attribute just because its default appearance seems convenient.

items.title: Width descriptors and pixel-density descriptors
items.text: The width attribute: the intrinsic display width in CSS pixels; dimensions help reserve layout space.

items.title: The <picture> element
items.text: Picture lets the browser choose among image sources for different formats or art direction, with img as fallback.

content_blocks.title: Keep in mind
content_blocks.text: Prefer the native semantic element that communicates intent. Do not choose markup solely for its default visual style.

content.task: Create a small HTML example that demonstrates responsive images. Keep the markup minimal, give every element a clear purpose, and inspect the rendered result.
task_acceptance_criteria: Use the relevant concept from Responsive Images.
Keep IDs unique and use valid nesting.
Check the result in a browser and record one finding.
hints: Start with the smallest valid example for responsive images.
Add one element or attribute at a time, then check the result.
Compare the source and rendered DOM if the behavior surprises you.

troubleshooting.symptom: The expected content does not appear.
troubleshooting.check: Confirm the file was saved with an .html extension and inspect its path and nesting.
Check the resolved URL and confirm the referenced file or external resource exists and allows the request.

troubleshooting.symptom: The page looks correct but the markup may be invalid.
troubleshooting.check: Run the Nu Html Checker and follow its first relevant diagnostic, then validate again.

common_mistakes.why: The default appearance is not the element’s main meaning and can make navigation or maintenance harder.
common_mistakes.fix: Choose the element that matches the content purpose, then use CSS for presentation.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a browser’s recovery means the source is valid
common_mistakes.why: Browsers often recover from malformed markup, which can hide defects and produce unexpected document structure.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect the rendered DOM and run a validator against the original source.

common_mistakes.why: Missing files, narrow viewports, keyboard access, invalid input, or other states can expose defects.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the expected state plus one realistic edge case and an accessibility path.

summary: Responsive Images is about expressing document structure or behavior intentionally.

Providing fallback images is one of the decisions covered by Responsive Images. Decide what the markup is meant to communicate, choose the native HTML structure that expresses that meaning, and verify the result in a browser or a relevant validation checklist. Avoid using an element or attribute just because its default appearance seems convenient.
Verify both markup and behavior; do not infer correctness from appearance alone.
